document_summary: Justia mirror of N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 (2025), the New Jersey statute limiting residential security deposits to 1.5 months' rent and capping annual increases in additional security at 10% of the current deposit.

rules.title: Limitation on amount of security deposit (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2)
rules.requirement: An owner or lessee may not require a security deposit of more than 1.5 times one month's rent for residential dwelling property. Any additional security collected from a tenant in a year may not exceed 10 percent of the current security deposit.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent maximum; additional annual security max 10% of current deposit
rules.coverage_conditions: Real property used for dwelling purposes; applies to owners or lessees collecting security from a tenant.
rules.interaction: State-wide rule; the document does not discuss municipal interaction.
rules.quoted_span: An owner or lessee may not require more than a sum equal to 1 1/2 times 1 month's rental according to the terms of contract, lease, or agreement as a security for the use or rental of real property used for dwelling purposes.
rules.extraction_notes: Original statute L.1971, c.223, s.4; amended by L.2003, c.188, s.5. Effective date set to 2003 as the year of the most recent amendment shown; the exact effective date of the current text is not given in the document. The document is a Justia mirror (secondary source) and carries a disclaimer that it may not be the most current version. Exemptions (e.g., owner-occupied buildings with two or fewer units under the Security Deposit Act) are not stated in this section and are not extracted.
